To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the intracellular composition and the distribution of protein-bound aminoazo dyes in the livers of rats are different for each aminoazo dye tested.

the livers of rats treated with the carcinogenic dye 3′-methy-4-dimethy-aminoazobenze were found to have increased protein and desoxypyentosenucleiic acid in the nuclei and increased pentosenucleiuc acid in the nuclear fractions and in the supernatant fluids, decreased protein and pentoseneucleiuc acid in both granule fractions, and decreased riboflavin content in the large granule fraction.

feeding rats 3′-Methyl-4-diaminoazobenzine, a powerful carcinogen, for four weeks produces changes in the composition and protein-bound dye content of the fractions of rat liver that are so similar to the changes in hepatic tumor that it is difficult to distinguish between the two tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
studies on the effects of feeding aminoazo dyes on the intracellular constituents of the liver.
the effect of feeding aminoazo dyes on the intracellular distribution and metabolism of protein, nucleic acid, and riboflavin.

the effect of feeding various carcinogenic and non-carcinogenie aminoazo dyes to rats on the intracellular chemical composition of the liver and on the intracellular distribution and binding of the dye.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intracellular distribution pattern of protein-bound aminoazo dyes does not reflect the carcinogenicity or lack of carcinogenicity of any of the four dyes studied.
the intracellular distribution pattern of protein-bound aminoazo dyes does not correlate with carcinogenicity.
the carcinogenicity or the lack of it of the aminoazo dyes is not related to their effect on the composition of the cell fractions of the liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the highly active carcinogen produced many of the characteristic alterations in the intracellular composition previously observed with a moderately active carcinogen and in addition induced a few additional changes.
the carcinogenic aminoazo dyes, when fed in equimolar amounts to rats for four weeks, produced many of their effects on the liver cell by binding to the intracellular constituents.
the carcinogens, 4-didimethylamino-azobenzene and 3′-methyldidimethylaminoaobenzene, induced many of the same intracellular changes in the liver as did the non-carcinogen, 4-aminoaobenzene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver is a complex organ and the changes that are induced by the feeding of aminoazo dyes are many.
3′-MeDAB is more potent carcinogen than 3,4-DAB, and it induces many of the changes seen with 3,4- DAB in a greater magnitude.
the carcinogens are able to produce changes in the intracellular composition which are similar to the changes produced by a carcinogen which is much more powerful than the one studied.
